events/736_qizhao/phases/0/narrative: Du Fu was born in 712 in Gongxian, Henan. His grandfather Du Shenyan was a famous poet of the early Tang. As a boy Du Fu set himself a rule: “Read ten thousand books, walk ten thousand miles.”
events/736_qizhao/phases/0/instruction: Click the things in the house to find out what the boy wants.
events/736_qizhao/phases/0/npcs/0/dialog: On the desk lie Du Shenyan's drafts — “Only a man far from home is startled when the season turns.”
Grandfather's poems are wide and open. Mine should be too.
events/736_qizhao/phases/0/npcs/1/dialog: Grandfather always said: read ten thousand books, walk ten thousand miles.
events/736_qizhao/phases/0/npcs/2/dialog: Zimei, reading again? They say the jinshi exam is on again this year.
I want to go out and see the world first.
events/736_qizhao/phases/1/transitionTex: In 735 Du Fu went to Luoyang to sit the jinshi exam…
events/736_qizhao/phases/1/announcement/: The list: Du Fu — not passed.
events/736_qizhao/phases/1/dufu_reaction: So I failed. The world is wide — is one list the whole of it?
events/736_qizhao/phases/2/title: The great journey through Qi and Zhao
events/736_qizhao/phases/2/travelNarrati: After failing, Du Fu set out from Luoyang and spent the next few years roaming Qi and Zhao.
events/736_qizhao/phases/2/instruction: Click each stop and hear what he says on the road.
events/736_qizhao/phases/2/waypoints/0/d: My father holds a post here. I'll see him first.
events/736_qizhao/phases/2/waypoints/1/d: What is Daizong like? Across Qi and Lu, green with no end…
events/736_qizhao/phases/2/waypoints/2/d: One day I will climb the highest peak, and see how small the mountains are!
(This is the moment Du Fu wrote “Gazing at the Peak.”)
events/736_qizhao/phases/3/poemContext: You are standing on the summit. The lines are almost out of you — put each word back into the right blank.
events/736_qizhao/phases/3/puzzle:
What is Daizong like? Across ___, green with no end.
Nature ___ every wonder here; ___ cut dusk from dawn.
Layered clouds ___ and stir my chest; I strain my eyes at birds coming home.
One day I will ___, and see ___.
events/736_qizhao/phases/4/transitionTex:
In five years
Du Fu crossed Qi, Zhao, Wu and Yue,
made bold friends, and set himself beside the great ministers of old.
events/736_qizhao/phases/4/dufu_reaction: Li Bai… I have read his poems for ten years. They say he is coming to Luoyang too.
quiz/736_qizhao/quizzes/0/explanation: Du Shenyan was one of the early Tang's “Four Friends of Letters.” Du Fu's gift for poetry ran in the family.
quiz/736_qizhao/quizzes/1/question: “One day I will climb the highest peak, and see how small the mountains are” — which mountain is this?
quiz/736_qizhao/quizzes/1/explanation: “Gazing at the Peak” is about Mount Tai, the Eastern Peak. “Daizong” is its old name.
quiz/736_qizhao/quizzes/2/question:
Fill in the famous line from “Gazing at the Peak”:
“Nature gathered every wonder here; ____ cut dusk from dawn.”
quiz/736_qizhao/quizzes/2/explanation: Shade and sun cut dusk from dawn — one side of the mountain is bright, the other dark. That is how huge Mount Tai is.
